free_tier.stated: Spark plan (no-cost): 10 test runs per day on virtual devices and 5 test runs per day on physical devices, 15 test runs per day in total; Blaze plan: 30 minutes of test time per day on physical devices and 60 minutes of test time per day on virtual devices at no cost, then USD 5 per hour for each physical device and USD 1 per hour for each virtual device, charged per minute rounded up; Android Device Streaming adds 30 no-cost minutes per project per month.
free_tier.notes: The Spark allowance is denominated in test runs per day, not in minutes; the Blaze allowance is denominated in test minutes per day. The two shapes are stated separately by the vendor. Android Device Streaming is a separate per-minute meter: 30 no-cost minutes per project per month, then USD 0.15 per additional minute on Blaze.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a device test, not an object; an APK uploaded to a test matrix is test input rather than a stored object

retention.stated: Test result summary is stored in the Firebase console and raw results in a Google Cloud bucket; no retention period is stated for either

egress.terms: not published as a quota or price: the page states that all network traffic generated by Test Lab devices originates from published IP address blocks, and that the user is responsible for the cost of a Cloud Storage bucket specified for raw results; if no bucket is specified, Test Lab creates one at no cost

interface_detail: The Firebase console, Android Studio integration, and the gcloud CLI run tests; the Cloud Testing API and Cloud Tool Results API are the programmatic surfaces, reached through the Google Cloud console for quota monitoring.
tooling: gcloud CLI, Android Studio, the Firebase console, and the Cloud Testing and Tool Results APIs; the gcloud beta firebase test ip-blocks list command prints the device egress ranges.
chaining: A device test is a short-lived compute job: the APK is supplied by a build pipeline, results land in a Cloud Storage bucket, and a matrix of devices multiplies the per-device hourly rate; the free daily test-run count is the quota that binds a Spark project.

limits.value: Spark: 10 virtual-device test runs and 5 physical-device test runs per day, 15 in total; Blaze: 60 virtual-device minutes and 30 physical-device minutes per day at no cost
Cloud Testing API: 10,000,000 calls per day and 120,000 calls per 1-minute interval; Cloud Tool Results API: 200,000 calls per day and 2,400 calls per 1-minute interval

limits_note: All test types are limited to 45 minutes on physical devices and 60 minutes on virtual devices; charges are per minute rounded up, so a 22-second test bills one minute and a 75-second test bills two. Quotas are project-level, shared across instrumentation, Robo and Game Loop tests and test matrices.
binding_note: The per-day test-run count (Spark) or the no-cost test-minute allowance (Blaze) is consumed by each device in a matrix before the much larger API call-rate ceilings are reached, and a matrix multiplies the count by the number of devices selected.

identity_cost.detail: A Firebase account is needed: on the no-cost Spark plan no payment information is needed to get started; the pay-as-you-go Blaze plan links a Cloud Billing account and, if eligible, offers USD 300 in free credit. Sign-in methods are Google, Apple, or email and password. No phone number or ID document is stated on the pricing pages.

reliability_note: Firebase Test Lab is deprecated and will be fully shut down as of September 30, 2027; Google directs users to the Developer Device Platform on Google Cloud. Physical devices are wiped and, where possible, flashed between test runs; virtual device instances are deleted after use; test types are capped at 45 minutes on physical and 60 minutes on virtual devices.
confidence_note: The rate card, the Spark and Blaze no-cost allowances, the per-minute rounding and the API ceilings are quoted from Google's own Test Lab usage, quotas and pricing page read 2026-11-24; the Spark/Blaze identity gate is from Firebase's own pricing-plans page; the shutdown date is from Google's release notes and deprecation FAQ.

notes: The no-cost quota is per project per day, not per identity, and it is shared across instrumentation, Robo and Game Loop tests. Each device in a test matrix consumes its own allowance, so a matrix of 10 virtual devices exhausts the Spark daily allowance in one run.
